blocks.text: Hypotheses are of different types, each with its own purpose. The two most common, the null and the alternative hypothesis, work together in every test, and correct hypotheses reduce confusion and improve the analysis.

blocks.caption: Null and alternative hypotheses
rows: No effect, difference or relationship (the default assumption)
There is an effect, difference or relationship (the opposite of H0)
The data is tested against it; it is rejected only if the evidence against it is strong. It gives a neutral base for comparison and helps avoid bias.
What the research usually hopes to support; it represents change or impact, and needs strong evidence.

blocks.title: Class activity
blocks.text: Write a null and an alternative hypothesis for a situation about marks or percentages, and discuss whether they are correct.

items: Research question: Does the amount of study time affect students' exam scores?
H0: There is no significant relationship between study time and exam scores.
H1: The amount of study time significantly affects students' exam scores.

blocks.alt: A box with the research question 'Does study time affect students' exam scores?' branches into two boxes: the null hypothesis H0 (no effect or difference: study time has no significant relationship with scores) and the alternative hypothesis H1 or Ha (an effect or difference: study time significantly affects scores). A note says the test starts by assuming H0, and strong evidence against it means rejecting H0 in favour of H1.
blocks.caption: A research question and its two hypotheses (original diagram after 7.2).
blocks.long_description: H0 and H1 must cover the possibilities between them, so that rejecting one points to the other.

items: Clear and specific: vague statements reduce accuracy.
Testable with data, with variables clearly defined.

blocks.text: Correctly formulated hypotheses save time and lead to reliable results.

blocks.prompt: A shop owner claims that a new display has increased average daily sales above Rs 20,000. Write H0 and H1.
blocks.explanation: H0: the average daily sales with the new display are Rs 20,000 or less (no increase). H1: the average daily sales are more than Rs 20,000.

items: H0: no effect or difference; the default that is tested.
H1 (Ha): there is an effect; supported only by strong evidence.
Good hypotheses are clear, specific, testable and match the question.
